event: 2025 ILCA 4 YOUTH EUROPEAN CHAMPIONSHIPS & OPEN EUROPEAN TROPHY
procedural_matters: Hearing Nº 40 was heard together with hearing No. 46 in accordance with RRS 63.2(b) since both hearings arose from the same incident.
The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
ITA 221824 was represented by Mattia Panvini.
ITA 220976 was represented by Lorenzo Savelli.
The race committee was represented by Michal Jodlowski (Course Race officer Area A).
Wojtek Jedliński, member of the international jury, attend the hearing as an observer.
Max Jablecki, member of the race committee, attend the hearing as an observer.
facts: In Race F1 of the ILCA Men silver fleet, the conditions were 5 knots of wind and flat water.
During leg 4 of the O2 course, the second upwind, a wind shift of more than 40º to the left occurred.
Before the wind shift reached the sailing area, the wind turbines onshore have rotated to a new wind direction.
The leg became a direct saiing on port tack to the mark number 2.
Before the wind shift, ITA 220976 was sailing around 20-25th place. ITA 220976 finished in 44th place.
Before the wind shift, ITA 221824 was sailing around 4th place. ITA 221824 finished in 34th place.
The Race Committee considered changing the course, but the wind shift occurred after the fleet had passed the gate.
The Race committee monitored the conditions which affected in a similar way the entire fleet.
The Race Committee did not abandon the race.

The Race Management Policies for World Sailing Events Fleet Racing states: ”With a persistent wind shift of more than 45°, the race committee will consider its influence on the race. Under these circumstances, the race committee may either change the course or abandon the race.”
conclusions: By considering the influence of the windshift on the race, the race committee did not make an improper action or omission in non abbandoning the race.
Since the windshift did not affect directly the fairness of the competition, the race committee did not make an improper action or omission in non abbandoning the race.
There was neither an improper action nor improper omission of the race committee. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(1) are not met.
